articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) of the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
This amendment updates previous authorizations concerning transactions related to Iran, though specific details of the changes were not immediately released.
The issuance aims to provide updated guidance to the public regarding permissible activities under the Iran sanctions program.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities for North Korea and DRC-Related Activities
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)-related activities.

For North Korea, the sanctions target 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in government-run IT worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK's unlawful weapons programs.
The action also included designations related to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, though specific details on these were not immediately provided in the initial announcement.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Reaches Settlement Agreement with OFAC
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. on October 27, 2026.
The settlement resolves potential civil liability for apparent violations of OFAC sanctions programs.
Further details regarding the nature of the violations and the terms of the settlement were made available in the enforcement information section of OFAC's website.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC on October 26, 2026.
These amendments aim to provide clearer guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their obligations under OFAC regulations.
The updated FAQs are intended to assist in compliance efforts and ensure proper reporting procedures are followed.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: On October 21, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting a network facilitating Iran's sanctions evasion and petroleum trade.

Concurrently, OFAC removed Belarusian national Andrei Alekseevich Rybakov and Chinese national Lu Hezheng, along with two China-based animation studios, from the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List under the Belarus and North Korea sanctions programs, respectively.

The action also included the issuance of new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions, authorizing certain wind-down activities through November 20, 2026, for the Iran-related licenses.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Designations and General Licenses Under Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA)
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations and the issuance of associated General Licenses under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.
These actions are part of a broader effort to counter technology transfer threats and protect American intellectual property.
The specific entities designated and the scope of the General Licenses were detailed in the official announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ for Earthquake Relief
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Venezuela-related General License (GL 60A) and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question on October 16, 2026.
This amendment extends the authorization for transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela, replacing and superseding the previous GL 60.
The authorization period has been extended from its original end date of October 23, 2026, to April 21, 2027, to facilitate ongoing humanitarian aid.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related and Cuba-Related Entities, Issues New General Licenses
body: On October 15, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, targeting 16 individuals and 10 entities for allegedly enabling sanctions evasion and sustaining Iran's military and proxy forces.

These designations included Iran-based banks Jazireh International Bank Company and Chabahar International Bank Overseas Company, operating offshore in free trade zones, as well as Iranian exchange houses and individuals involved in foreign exchange operations.
Additionally, OFAC issued a Cuba designation and new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions, further implementing sanctions related to Executive Order 14404.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan Politician Jorge Rodriguez from Sanctions List
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) removed Jorge Rodriguez, the head of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list on October 14, 2026.
This delisting ends the associated asset freeze and removes obstacles for U.S. persons attempting to deal with him.
Rodriguez, who has served as President of Venezuela's National Assembly since 2021, was initially designated in 2018 under the Trump administration.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: On October 13, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations.

This action targeted four individuals and 11 entities allegedly linked to Cartel del Noreste (CDN), a Mexico-based cartel designated as both a Foreign Terrorist Organization and a Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT).

According to the Treasury Department, this represents OFAC's largest sanctions action to date targeting CDN, imposed pursuant to Executive Order 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production, and Executive Order 13224, as amended, which targets terrorists and their supporters.

articles.headline: EU Adopts 22nd Sanctions Package Against Russia, Designating Nearly 1,600 Individuals and Entities
body: On October 12, 2026, the European Union adopted its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, adding 1,569 individuals and entities to its sanctions lists.

This package, implemented through Council Decision (CFSP) 2026/2279 and Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2281, includes 826 Russian companies and 743 individuals, bringing the total number of designations under the Ukraine-related sanctions regime to almost 4,600.

The measures primarily target Russia's military-industrial complex, including companies involved in the production and supply of components for missiles, drones, and military aircraft, as well as individuals involved in the recent Russian legislative elections held in occupied Ukrainian territories.

articles.headline: EU Adds Three Individuals and Four Entities to DPRK Sanctions List
body: The Council of the European Union adopted additional restrictive measures against three individuals and four entities under its autonomous sanctions list on the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) on October 12, 2026.

These designations target those responsible for supporting, promoting, or facilitating activities that contribute to the DPRK's programs related to nuclear weapons, ballistic missiles, or other weapons of mass destruction, as well as for violating and evading United Nations sanctions.

The new listings also address activities linked to the growing military and economic cooperation between the DPRK and Russia, including the deployment of DPRK workers in Russia and commercial and industrial cooperation.

articles.headline: UK Updates Sanctions List with Variation for Russia Regime
body: On October 29, 2026, the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office updated the UK Sanctions List on GOV.UK with a variation under the Russia regime.

This variation signifies a change to an existing designation following an official decision-making process, with deleted information appearing in strikethrough and newly added information underlined and highlighted.
The update includes changes related to entities carrying on business in the Russian energy sector, such as Litasco Middle East DMCC and Litasco SA.

articles.headline: UN General Assembly Condemns US Embargo on Cuba for 34th Consecutive Year
body: The United Nations General Assembly voted on October 28, 2026, to condemn the decades-long U.S. embargo against Cuba for the 34th consecutive year.
The resolution, which demands an end to the economic, commercial, and financial blockade, was adopted with 130 votes in favor, 17 against, and 25 abstentions.
The vote underscores Washington's continued isolation over a policy widely criticized for violating international law and inflicting hardship on the Cuban people.

articles.headline: U.S. Bans Imports from Three Chinese Genomics Companies Over Xinjiang Forced Labor Allegations
body: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced on October 28, 2026, that it is blocking imports from three Chinese biotech companies—BGI Group, BGI Genomics, and MGI Tech—alleging ties to forced labor in China's Xinjiang region.
These companies have been added to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List, which imposes U.S. import bans on goods presumed to be made with forced labor.
DHS stated that these firms have supported genetic testing in Xinjiang, which facilitates the monitoring, surveillance, and repression of ethnic minorities, including the practice of forced labor.
articles.source: U.S. Department of Homeland Security / Reuters

articles.headline: Bank of America, N.A. Pays $11,662,930 in OFAC Civil Penalty
body: Bank of America, N.A. has settled with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for $11,662,930.

This penalty is part of a larger enforcement action by the Treasury Department, which also included significant penalties from FinCEN and the OCC, totaling over $1.21 billion for anti-money laundering and sanctions violations.

The OFAC settlement addresses 475 apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs, occurring when the bank channeled correspondent banking payments through blocked banks, allowed designated individuals to make payments, and failed to update watchlists and handle accounts associated with blocked persons.

articles.headline: OCC Announces Enforcement Actions for October 2026, Including Significant Penalties
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released its enforcement actions for October 2026 on October 22, 2026, detailing various penalties against financial institutions and individuals.

Among the actions, American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah, received a Cease and Desist Order and a $350 million civil money penalty for deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance program, including failures to timely file suspicious activity reports and violations of customer due diligence and customer identification program requirements.

Additionally, the OCC issued Orders of Prohibition against Jennifer Hamblin, a Vault Teller at Fifth Third Bank, N.A., for embezzling approximately $292,000 in customer funds, and Christopher Organista, a Former Operations Processor at U.S. Bank National Association, for embezzling approximately $194,131 in bank customer funds.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.

articles.headline: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
body: The order comes after election officials received letters demanding they set aside the ballots of possible non-citizen voters.

articles.headline: What Florida jet audio and flight data tells us about its final moments
body: A private jet crashed in Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people on board, according to US authorities.
